page.description: FreeDOS editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: An open-source, MS-DOS-compatible operating system for PCs, still released and still able to run DOS programs and games on real hardware or in a virtual machine.
pros: Runs DOS programs and games on period hardware and in virtual machines.
Free, open source and actively maintained, with monthly test builds.
Media for CD, USB, floppy and virtual machines.
A 20 MB disk is enough for a plain installation.
cons: Needs BIOS or UEFI in Legacy mode: no native UEFI and no Secure Boot.
The USB and CD media ship as ZIP archives, so ROMinit pins no image.
The kernel is still the 1.3 one; a new kernel is only in test builds.
Single-tasking DOS: no memory protection and no modern drivers.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for FreeDOS; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: The project publishes its media as ZIP archives containing the bootable images: unzip first, then write the contained image. ROMinit does not pin an archive here; the download page names which package fits CD, USB or floppy.
